Tanya: "We shipped the async decision widget. Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter. The Zephyr integration was the key unlock."

payload.focus: Sprint retro: async decision widget shipped, velocity 23 points highest this quarter, Zephyr integration as key unlock
payload.rationale: This sprint retro directly extends the prior Sprint 4 retro (Sample_Sprint4Retro_20260322) and its positions: Position_ZephyrIntegrationUnlock (Zephyr as key unlock), Obs_TinaVelocity (23-point velocity claim), Position_Sprint4ThesisProven (thesis proven by widget), StyleObs_Sprint4_MetricAnchor (numeric anchoring style), and Obs_ZephyrRateLimitResolved (blocker cleared). The async decision widget is the productization of Position_CoreFeatureDecisionCapture and Narrative_DecisionCaptureAtConsensus, so those narratives and positions must be surfaced for the passes to bind this retro to the product thesis. Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning and its children (Position_AntiPatternRealtimeChat, Position_ProductCategoryAsyncPlatform) frame the anti-Slack positioning the widget embodies. Position_PricingTwelveDollars is included because the Sprint 4 retro records a pricing update to $15/user, and this document may bear on that thread. Narrative_DecisionsEvaporate is the foundational problem narrative the widget solves. I did not expand Position_TargetMarketRemoteTeams or Position_ContextPreservationNextSprint — the document does not touch target market sizing or next-sprint planning.

The map and index never vary with your focus; your per-call material is at the end.

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). Decide from the map; expand to ground.
